correctness.rationale: For M>=3 Xie Theorem 1.1 yields an integral codimension-three complete intersection. Directly, the Jacobian is dependent iff VΛ=0 for a nonzero hollow symmetric Λ, which must have rank>=2. Rank(V)>=2 is therefore smooth. Rank-one V=w(c1,c2,c3) is singular iff det(c-relation)=-2c1c2c3=0. This exhaustively identifies three linear and three isotropic rank-one components. Each isotropic cone is Segre(P1×Q^{M-2}) of dimension M and degree 2(M-1). At a dense open set of each linear component, two regular equations leave the nondegenerate pairing on (M-1)+(M-1) variables; the same happens on each isotropic component after separating v3=c v2+y and solving two equations. Formal Morse lemma with parameters proves the generic ordinary quadratic germ. Packaged verifier checked Jacobian rank two and tangent-space Hessian rank 2M-2 for both types at M=3,4,5,6, and determinant identities; finite tests do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Material readings of the three closest primary treatments establish general ideal, rationality, and normality results but do not state or imply the exact decomposition of the reduced singular locus of the three-vector zero fiber into six M-dimensional components, the combined degree 6M-3, and all six generic quadratic analytic normal forms. Seven actual targeted semantic mathematical-record searches and primary-literature searches produced no equivalent statement. Generic Jacobian and Segre techniques are known; their exact resulting theorem for this Gram family is the object evaluated. Broad unindexed singular-stratification results remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: The first full-rational-singularity three-vector Gram family has a natural unresolved geometric gap between global normality/rationality and concrete singular stratification. Exact six-component equidimensional support, individual degrees 1 and 2(M-1), total degree 6M-3, and generic analytic quadratic type classify intrinsic degeneracies for every dimension, with plausible application to local invariants and resolution questions. This is more than a singularity check or small numerical gain and is not inferred from existing FRS thresholds. The result deliberately does not claim the Jacobian scheme or complicated component-intersection germs.
